about: SnapshotInterpolationBuffer, replayed step by step: each add gives the sample's server time, local arrival, x and x velocity (float32 bits, velocity null when absent) and the result; each frame gives the local time, render time, mode, x, target delay and playback offset after the frame. Delay: the longer of the interval estimate and the largest gap between buffered samples (ignoring gaps that span a dropped sample), plus three jitters, clamped to 80-350 ms. The playback offset (render time minus local time) moves toward offset minus delay by at most 10% of elapsed local time; while offset minus playback offset exceeds 400 ms (the 350 ms cap plus a 50 ms dead band), one percent more per millisecond beyond 400 ms, up to 100%; while it is below the 80 ms floor, one percent more per millisecond below it, up to 50%. The render time is then floored at the last render time, and the playback offset follows it. A full buffer of 20 drops its oldest sample, the next one if the render holds the oldest, or the third if the render is between the oldest two. Samples arriving together go in by server time. Y and z are zero and rotations identity.

scenarios.name: a late sample never pauses playback
uneven cadence is covered by the delay
jitter, a duplicate, a stale sample and a timeline reset
a 900 ms timeline step is caught up
a 300 ms latency drop at 20 Hz stays in the dead band
a resend older than the full buffer, then a 100 ms latency rise at 30 Hz
